rationale: Evidence from direct case reports and reviews of dHMN caused by heterozygous SPTAN1 variants (dHMN11) demonstrates that reflex loss is not generalized into pan-areflexia. Instead, patients characteristically exhibit dissociated lower extremity reflexes, maintaining brisk/hyperactive patellar reflexes (e.g., graded +++) and extensor plantar responses (Babinski signs) alongside distal lower limb denervation/weakness and absent ankle jerks. This reflects upper motor neuron/pyramidal tract involvement coexisting with length-dependent distal motor axonopathy.

evidence.text: In a Chinese family with dHMN caused by a novel de novo SPTAN1 nonsense variant, neurological examination revealed brisk/hyperactive knee reflexes (+++) and positive Babinski sign on the left, demonstrating proximal reflex preservation/hyperactivity rather than pan-areflexia.

evidence.text: Screening of a 128-patient cohort with distal hereditary motor neuropathy, which identified causative variants across cytoskeleton-related genes including SPTAN1, found that pyramidal impairments (such as hyperreflexia) were present in 11 of 128 individuals, highlighting the presence of upper motor signs in motor neuropathy phenotypes.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of hyperactive patellar reflexes in SPTAN1-associated neuropathy correlate strictly with specific functional domains (e.g., spectrin repeats vs. actin-binding domain)?
new_directions.rationale: Determining genotype-phenotype correlations between truncation/nonsense variants causing pure dHMN versus missense variants causing hereditary spastic paraplegia can clarify why pyramidal disinhibition spares patellar reflexes.
